statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk is 20%, the floor of the watch band, after the Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,501.56 having fully recovered its morning low, while Stress stays high at 74% on a 24-year-peak yield backdrop and Brent above $100.

headline: Nasdaq-100 closes a fully retraced session as yields retreat from a 24-year peak, while Brent above $100 keeps Stress high
body: Verified evidence at the assessment cutoff covers a completed US cash session. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,501.56, up 93.06 points or 0.31% against a 30,408.50 previous close, inside a 30,274.65-30,616.24 range. The structural fact that matters most is the shape of that session: the index opened higher, sank to its session low as long-end yields climbed, and then recovered through the afternoon as yields eased. The close sits 115 points below the session high, 227 points above the low and 269 points below the 52-week high of 30,770.63, so the index finished in the upper half of its range rather than pinned at an extreme, and the morning decline was fully retraced. Implied volatility closed at 16.45, up 0.67%, having decayed from a 17.59 session high toward the 16.21 low. The Treasury curve richened across maturities after an extreme intraday move: the 2-year ended at 4.79% (-11.7bp), the 5-year at 5.01% (-9bp), the 10-year at 5.24% (-5bp) after touching 5.34%, its highest since 2002, and the 30-year at 5.61% (-2.5bp); the quarter just closed was the bond market's worst this century. Energy is the one aligned amplifier and the escalation is new: Brent gained 4.36% to $102.30 and WTI 2.73% to $92.89 after the Wall Street Journal reported that the United States is sending a third aircraft carrier strike group to the Middle East, with arrival and up to 10,000 additional troops expected by late November, while Iran loaded no crude onto tankers in September under the existing naval blockade. Today's US releases were firm: initial jobless claims 197,000, a fourth consecutive weekly decline, continuing claims 1.701 million, ISM Manufacturing 54.5 with new orders at 55.3, production at 56.7 and employment at 52.7, and construction spending up 0.9%. The ISM prices index jumped 6.8 points to 77.9%, which is the inflation backdrop for tomorrow's wage data. Semiconductor tone is supportive after Micron's record $54.23 billion quarter, $33.42 adjusted earnings per share and guidance of about $61.5 billion, though the shares themselves barely moved. Because yields retreated, volatility decayed and the session produced a genuine retracement, the amplifier set is not aligned and Tail holds the 20% watch floor while Stress stays high at 74%. NQ futures are inside their 20:00-21:00Z daily halt, so the delayed futures quote near 30,812 is context rather than live path evidence. The shared Finviz context file was roughly 45 hours old and marked partial, so it was excluded and this assessment rests on independently verified sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hours are available from published Claude assessments. Tail ranged 20-25% and the mapped state was WATCH in 23 of the 24 hours, with a single orange BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES hour at 06:00Z when Tail touched 25% during a trend-up European phase. Stress rose from 70% overnight to a 78% peak across 14:00-15:00Z as the global bond selloff pushed the 10-year to a 24-year high, then eased to 74-76% as yields retreated into the close. Confidence held 87-89% throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast window holds the watch band through the futures halt, the Asian session and the European morning, with Tail at 20-22% and dominant mode normal to mixed while China's National Day holiday thins regional flow. Risk then builds into 2 October: Tail reaches 24% for the 12:30Z September employment report and 25% for the 13:30Z cash open, the single orange hour inside the narrow danger window, before easing to 21-24% as post-event price discovery is scored. Stress peaks at 79% around the release and returns to 74% by 18:00Z, ticking the final cash hour back to Tail 22% on weekend risk reduction.
